title: Show scope, never ask for scrolling
intent: Tell the user where they are and how far the surface goes, instead of instructing them to move.
when_to_use: a surface is longer than one viewport and the user needs to know its extent
several regions compete for the same screen
when_not_to_use: the page is a single message that fits one viewport, where any scope indicator is chrome
the surface is a document read linearly, where the browser already reports position
rules: the page contains no instruction to move down, no down arrow, and no animated cue pointing past the fold
the current region is named in a persistent element that states the total when the content is finite
below fold content is announced by its own title, never by a teaser line or a partially cut card
any position indicator is text or a measured value, never a decorative dot
trade_off: You lose the cheap drama of a cut off element implying more, and a page whose second section is weak has nothing to hide behind.
failure_mode: Scope turns into ornament: a dot rail with no labels, a sticky bar repeating the page title, and a progress bar on a page that has no steps.

example.brief: Long settings surface with eight grouped sections.
example.ruling: A persistent group list states the eight groups and marks the current one, the last group is preceded by a count of remaining items, and the down arrow in the hero is deleted.
